title: Garage Door Spam
author: harrisonpage
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: In the beginning, my garage door opener worked fine. When the door opened or closed, I would get a notification. If I'm away from home and the door opens, something weird is going down. The "myQ" app generally worked although it was encrusted with ads:
I continued using it because I trusted that notifications were meaningful... ...until recently (October 2026):

This is un-fucking-acceptable. As in, absolutely fucking not. The manufacturer (Chamberlain) cut off third-party access to its APIs (via myQ) in late 2023. In response, I purchased a pair of ratgdo32 devices to opt out of the bullshit.
ratgdo is a WiFi control board for your garage door opener that works over your local network using ESP Home or HomeKit

comments.author: AceJohnny2
comments.textRawHtml:
The Apple App Store Review Guidelines 4.5.4 [1] have this to say:

> Push Notifications must not be required for the app to function, and should not be used to send sensitive personal or confidential information. Push Notifications should not be used for promotions or direct marketing purposes unless customers have explicitly opted in to receive them via consent language displayed in your app’s UI, and you provide a method in your app for a user to opt out from receiving such messages. Abuse of these services may result in revocation of your privileges.

I am frustrated that Apple isn't using their gatekeeping powers for good. I wonder if users can file a complaint.

[1] https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/#des...

Edit: yes, users can file complaints. If you are an Apple Developer, you can do so via https://developer.apple.com/help/app-review/safe-and-trusted...

You can also follow "Report A Problem" link at the bottom of the App Store's page for the app.

children.author: trestacos
children.textRawHtml:
We really need to start moving to app platforms that give you more control over notifications. It's really disappointing that developers are bundling their marketing and "useful" notifications and apple does nothing about it. At this point, apple knows developers do this and doesn't do anything about it.

What would this look like? Web apps that give you more control over what specific notifications you get.

children.author: tonic_note
children.textRawHtml:
Yeah, this is the thing that I think everyone misses when they talk about how notifications on iOS are fucked. They're always quibbling over the grouping, the presentation, and the organization, but what actually needs to happen is the user needs to be given full granular control over every single type of notification that an app can send. Apps should be required to catalog every single notification, and I should be able to choose which ones I want.

There are tons of useful notifications I would like to get, but I end up having to choose the nuclear option of turning them off completely because I know that by allowing notifications, I expose myself to vomit-inducing growth hack spam.

children.author: miki123211
children.textRawHtml:
In many jurisdictions, phone companies are legally barred from refusing service to anybody.

They're a common carrier, you wouldn't want an automated fraud detection system to accidentally flag you and prevent you from ever obtaining another phone number in your country again.

This is the other side of the "why is Meta banning innocent people" coin. We could prevent Meta from doing this by law. What would the consequences be? I don't know, but I know that your car warranty has expired, are you interested in renewing it?

children.author: thaumasiotes
children.textRawHtml:
I don't understand your response. In the first place, messaging services aren't phone companies.

But if we assume that they are, all that would mean is that anyone is entitled to register a WhatsApp account. It wouldn't mean - could never mean - that anyone with a WhatsApp account is entitled to have their messages seen by anyone else they try to communicate with. Whether I take your call is between you and me, not between you and the phone company.

children.author: eloisius
children.textRawHtml:
I’ve wished for this for a decade, so I don’t imagine it’s coming any time soon, but 100 times, yes. And it should require some kind of non-totality-generic template string to register a notification, otherwise developers would just register a global

    %message%
template and continue to send their “time-sensitive” emoji slurry of marketing messages.

children.author: joe_fishfish
children.textRawHtml:
Android has per-app notification channels that let you mute notifications by category for each app.

Sadly, the biggest Android OEM (Samsung) has decided to hide this feature in the settings app, meaning lots of users don't even know about it.

It also requires app developers to categorise their push notifications themselves, which they often refuse to do, despite Play Store guidelines requiring it.

children.author: miki123211
children.textRawHtml:
This works against notifications being informative, though.

The best push notification is one that I don't have to click. "Your package from Apple has just been delivered". is infinitely better than "new activity on one of your deliveries, click to learn more."

We don't want companies optimizing for max(open rate) because that encourages the latter style.
